title: Free Trials That Actually Include Social Listening (2026)
summary: A free trial isn't the same as a testable listening feature. Compare 12 social listening tools — Awario, Sprout Social, Hootsuite, and more — for 2026.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** A free trial existing is not the same as the Listening feature itself being testable. Of the 12 social listening tools in this benchmark, five let you sign up without a sales call — Awario (7 days), Brand24 (14 days), Determ (5 days), Sprout Social (30 days), and Agorapulse — but Sprout Social's trial excludes Listening entirely (it's an unpriced paid add-on) and Agorapulse gates it behind a separate, manually-activated 30-day trial with its own volume caps. Hootsuite's 14-day trial never includes Listening at all, since "advanced listening" sits behind Hootsuite's Enterprise tier. Every enterprise vendor checked here — Brandwatch, Meltwater, Talkwalker, Sprinklr, Quid, and Onclusive Social — requires a sales demo before any hands-on access.


Ask a vendor if they offer a free trial, and most will say yes. Ask whether that trial actually lets you test the Listening feature — the thing you're there to evaluate in the first place — and the answer gets a lot murkier. That gap between "there's a trial" and "the trial tests what I need" turned out to be the most useful, least-covered finding in this research: several of the biggest self-serve social listening platforms sell Listening as a separate, unpriced add-on that the standard trial simply doesn't include.


That matters because trial access is the cheapest way to de-risk a listening purchase before committing budget to it, and a trial that quietly excludes the core feature isn't really a trial of that feature at all. This benchmark checked the actual signup flow, trial length, credit-card requirement, and — critically — whether Listening itself is included, for 12 vendors ranging from entry-tier self-serve tools to quote-only enterprise platforms. For the pricing side of this same question — what these tools cost once you're past the trial — see our[social listening pricing benchmarks](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-pricing-benchmarks-2026-what-brands-actually-pay-by-tier) .


## Which social listening tools offer a genuinely self-serve free trial, no sales call required?


Five vendors in this research let you start a trial yourself, right now, without talking to sales first: Awario, Brand24, Determ, Sprout Social, and Agorapulse. Syncly Social also offers self-serve signup with no demo requirement.


-


**Awario** — confirmed 7-day trial, no credit card required (Source:[Awario Help, 2026](https://awario.com/help/troubleshooting/trial-and-demonstration/) ). Note: this corrects a 14-day figure that appeared in an earlier post in this series — Awario's own help center confirms 7 days.


-


**Brand24** — 14-day trial, no credit card (Source:[Brand24 Pricing, 2026](https://brand24.com/pricing/) ).


-


**Determ** — 5-day trial (Source:[Determ Free Trial, 2026](https://determ.com/free-trial/) ).


-


**Sprout Social** — 30-day trial, no credit card (Source:[Sprout Social Trial, 2026](https://sproutsocial.com/trial/) ) — but the length doesn't tell the whole story, covered below.


-


**Agorapulse** — the base plan trial is self-serve, though Listening itself needs a second, separate activation step (also below).


-


**Syncly Social** — self-serve signup, no demo required to start.


No enterprise-tier vendor in this research offers a trial that skips the sales call — that pattern is covered in full further down.


## Does the free trial actually include the Listening feature, or is that gated separately?


This is the finding that matters most: a trial existing and the Listening feature being testable are two different things, and two of the biggest self-serve platforms in this category keep them separate.


**Feature-gated trial** : a free trial that grants access to a product's general shell — publishing, scheduling, a basic dashboard — but excludes the specific capability a prospect most needs to evaluate, either because that capability is sold as a separate paid add-on or reserved for a tier the trial doesn't reach. A **feature-complete trial** , by contrast, lets you exercise the exact capability you came to test.

Three cases are worth walking through individually.


**Sprout Social** promotes a 30-day, no-credit-card trial front and center — but Social Listening itself is confirmed as a paid add-on that isn't bundled into any standard plan, meaning the headline 30-day number doesn't let a prospect test listening specifically without a separate purchase conversation (Source:[Sprout Social Trial, 2026](https://sproutsocial.com/trial/) ;[Sprout Social Pricing, 2026](https://sproutsocial.com/pricing/) — "Premium Analytics and Listening are each available as individual add-ons to the Standard plan and up").


**Agorapulse** requires navigating specifically to its Listening tool and clicking "Start your free trial" there — it's not automatic with base signup. Once activated, the Advanced Listening trial runs 30 days but is capped at 1,500 items per search and 10,000 items total, and it's available on all plans except Free (Source:[Agorapulse Help, 2026](https://support.agorapulse.com/en/articles/11384539-how-to-trial-the-advanced-listening-feature) ).


**Hootsuite's** own plans page markets "advanced listening" — trend detection across social, digital, and AI — as an Enterprise-only capability. A prospect on Hootsuite's confirmed 14-day, no-credit-card trial of Standard or Professional never actually reaches the listening product itself, only the publishing and scheduling shell around it (Source:[Hootsuite Plans, 2026](https://www.hootsuite.com/plans) ).


Awario and Brand24 are the contrast case: both include real[monitoring data](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) directly in the standard trial, with no separate activation step required.


## What data volume or feature caps apply during a free trial?


Every self-serve trial in this research caps something — mention volume, alert count, or search count — rather than offering unlimited access, and the size of that cap is itself a useful signal of how much real testing the trial allows.


-


**Awario** caps the 7-day trial at 3 alerts and up to 30,000 mentions (Source:[Awario Help, 2026](https://awario.com/help/troubleshooting/trial-and-demonstration/) ).


-


**Agorapulse's** Advanced Listening trial caps at 1,500 items per search and 10,000 items total, with one free Advanced Listening search allowed (unlimited edits to that one search) (Source:[Agorapulse Help, 2026](https://support.agorapulse.com/en/articles/11384539-how-to-trial-the-advanced-listening-feature) ).


-


**Determ's** trial is described by the vendor as "full-feature" for its 5 days rather than volume-capped (Source: search aggregation, 2026) — this wasn't independently re-verified beyond the day-count confirmation, so treat it as directionally accurate rather than fully confirmed.


-


**Brand24** and **Sprout Social** don't publish specific volume caps for trial accounts anywhere we could find — worth confirming directly with the vendor rather than assuming unlimited access.


## Which social listening tools only offer a demo, not a real trial?


Every enterprise-tier vendor checked in this research requires booking a sales demo before any hands-on access, with no self-serve signup path at any tier.


-


**Meltwater** — "Request a Demo" is the only entry point; no self-serve trial or free version exists, and the typical minimum contract runs 12 months (Source:[Meltwater Request a Demo, 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/request-demo) ;[Meltwater Pricing, 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/pricing) — "minimum contract length of 12 months").


-


**Brandwatch** — a direct fetch of Brandwatch's own plans page this session confirms the primary call-to-action across every tier is a demo-scheduling form, not a signup flow — there's no "start trial" or checkout path anywhere on the page, only "Schedule your free demo." Some third-party listicles claim a "30-day free trial," but no working self-serve signup path exists on Brandwatch's site to support that claim, so Brandwatch requires a demo rather than offering true self-serve access (Source:[Brandwatch Plans, 2026](https://www.brandwatch.com/plans/) ).


-


**Talkwalker, Sprinklr, Quid (formerly NetBase Quid), and Onclusive Social (formerly Digimind)** — all confirmed demo-only, with no self-serve tier at any price point. Talkwalker was directly spot-checked this session — its pricing page routes every plan to "Request a custom demo" with no self-serve signup option; Sprinklr, Quid, and Onclusive Social's demo-only status is reused from prior, consistent pipeline research rather than freshly re-verified line by line (Source:[Talkwalker Pricing, 2026](https://www.talkwalker.com/pricing) ; search aggregation, 2026 for the remaining three).


This tracks with a broader pattern: enterprise listening vendors are quote-only on pricing too, and that same opacity extends to how you're even allowed to see the product before buying.


## What this means for buyers


Before you sign up for any social listening trial, ask one question the vendor's marketing page won't answer for you: does this trial include Listening itself, or just the shell around it?


A few checks worth making before you rely on a "free trial" claim in your evaluation:


1.


**Confirm Listening is inside the trial, not an add-on.** If a vendor's pricing page lists "Listening" as a named feature without a price next to it, assume it isn't in the base trial until you've confirmed otherwise in writing.


2.


**Ask for the actual volume cap.** A trial capped at a few thousand mentions won't tell you much about how the tool performs on your real[competitor analysis](https://syncly.app/social/solution/competitor-analysis) or campaign-monitoring use case — find out the cap before you burn your trial window on a query that's too broad.


3.


**Don't assume "self-serve" means "feature-complete."** Agorapulse and Sprout Social both let you sign up in minutes; neither hands you a testable Listening feature by default.


4.


**Weigh what you're actually testing.** A trial that only exercises publishing and scheduling tells you nothing about listening accuracy, coverage, or how well the tool surfaces genuine[customer conversations](https://syncly.app/social/feature/conversation-insights) in the content types your audience actually posts in — video included.


Syncly Social's differentiator here isn't trial length — it's self-serve signup with no demo required, on a trial that tests the same[Audio Intelligence](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) speech-to-text and AI Vision on-screen detection the paid product runs, rather than a shell product with Listening carved out. Pricing is custom and quoted directly, in line with how this category generally prices past the entry tier.


## Key Takeaways


-


A free trial existing and the Listening feature being testable are two different things — Sprout Social and Agorapulse both offer self-serve trials that don't include Listening by default.


-


Awario (7 days), Brand24 (14 days), and Determ (5 days) are the cleanest feature-complete trials in this research — Listening data is available from signup, no separate activation.


-


Hootsuite's 14-day trial never reaches Listening at all, since "advanced listening" sits behind Hootsuite's Enterprise tier exclusively.


-


Every self-serve trial caps something — mentions, alerts, or searches — and the cap is a meaningful signal of how much real testing it allows.


-


Enterprise vendors (Brandwatch, Meltwater, Talkwalker, Sprinklr, Quid, Onclusive Social) require a sales demo before any hands-on access, full stop.


The honest read on free trials in this category: most vendors will let you sign up, but far fewer will let you actually test the feature you came to evaluate. Before you burn a trial window, confirm which one you're getting.
